doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Grammar and pronunciation inherited from her father
summary: Her father's expertise in English, mispronounced words and a funny literal anecdote.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You seem to be very attuned to good grammar and punctuation and — why?
I mean that’s, everybody should be, right?

That’s the short answer, my father. I remember when I was waitressing he said that it’s crème de manthe not crème de menthe — I said, “Daddy, that’s not the way the other waitresses pronounce it.” And he said, “And you should say langerie not lingerie. Why that came up I don’t remember. But nobody says langerie, an English speaker. And he was — he was an expert in the English language and that was the only subject I was ever good at in school, really. I was terrible at history, geography, chemistry. But I loved diagramming sentences. And I’m not saying that my grammar is perfect, my English is perfect, it’s not. I mean have you ever discovered that you’ve been mispronouncing a word for your entire life?
I did like Hardon, Bason and whatever that other one was.
That one, yeah. Well I found out that the word E-S-C-H-E-U apparently is pronounced “eschew.” I always thought it was askew. Like A-S-K —

Well we both have to look it up just to double check. But I’m pretty sure it’s not askew. But yeah, I got that from my dad and I’m happy that we had that in common. He called me once, this is shortly after I got married and he was laughing so hard he almost couldn’t talk, he said, “Lorraine I saw this anec — I won’t tell you who the actor was — this interview with a TV actor in TV Guide and he said he had taken up directing and he said, ‘One day I was sitting at my desk and I felt the desire to act literally drain through my fingertips.’ Literally.”
I can see how that would get to your father.
You know I have his — in case you notice, I have his early book strategically placed over my shoulder.
I can’t see them but thank you for showing me.
